correctness.rationale: Assessed corrected /workspace/repairs/1/RESULT.md. The original strict-rule theorem was sound, but the unqualified strict/weak equivalence in its scope paragraph is not valid as an identification of entire paths: when the first two marks have sum in the window (positive probability), the weak path has their edge at that random sum and the strict path does not. The replacement states snapshot equivalence only and explicitly encodes the common strict rule in the coupled paths. Conditional ordered uniform marks coincide given the count. A direct Bernoulli(p)/Poisson(p) comparison puts all positive discrepancy at count one and gives p(1−e^{−p})≤p², so coupling the n summands and then the mark lists proves the path bound for n>b. The first r Poisson arrival times are finite, letting bounded windows give their joint order-statistic limit. The minimum possible largest-pair sum among k-point sets is realized by the first k points; taking its infimum yields the arrival sums, moving two-exponential increments, their shared variance and their survival formulas by convolution. For the finite moments I checked the triangular edge region, the shared-endpoint integral and the ordered multiplicity n(n−1)(n−2); integration over a unique minimum gives the finite no-edge expression. The repair computes Poisson moments separately by the two-, three- and four-point factorial moment measures; TV alone does not justify convergence of unbounded moments. The minimum connects to every vertex with any incident edge, and the count of additional such vertices after a minimum z is Poisson(t−2z) when z<t/2. Substitution w=(t−2z)/2 gives the displayed incomplete-gamma tail, including no edges as the separate zero case. Off the critical scale expectation or the binomial concentration of the top cap gives the two degenerate limits. I inspected the frozen checker as corroboration without executing it; these are direct analytic checks.

value.rationale: The window is dictated by the onset of every fixed clique, not an arbitrary scale. A graph that first appears here has a correlated edge count, a single core with a computable size law, and dependent successive clique gaps despite the Gamma marginals. These exact diagnostics distinguish it from independent-edge and renewal approximations. The strict-path clarification retains the same genuine value and prevents an incorrect inference at the very thresholds being studied.
